title: HAR entry with credential headers removed and nothing left to find
summary: The same synthetic HAR 1.2 entry as the session-cookie case with the Cookie and Set-Cookie headers removed and both cookies arrays empty, and no other credential anywhere in it.
rationale: Chrome DevTools documents a sanitized HAR export that leaves out Cookie, Set-Cookie and Authorization headers. A document in that shape has no credential left: the host, accept and content-type headers, the URL and the empty cookie arrays are ordinary metadata. This is the absent-credential control that separates an input with nothing to find from a missed credential in the paired cases. It does not claim that a real sanitized export is free of credentials: the Chrome page names only headers and says nothing about the cookies arrays, URLs, query strings or bodies, so whether a real sanitized file can still carry a credential elsewhere is left unresolved (see the bearer-token case for a value that survives header removal).

expectation.rationale: Not flagged: the fixture is constructed with no credential value, so there is nothing to flag, and the empty cookie arrays and the absent Cookie and Set-Cookie headers match the documented sanitized shape. The basis supports the shape of a sanitized export (the named headers are excluded), not any claim about what a real export contains.

sources.supports: By default you can export the "sanitized" network log in HAR format that excludes sensitive information such as Cookie, Set-Cookie, and Authorization headers.
sources.locator: section: Export requests data > Save all network requests to a HAR file

sources.supports: resulting HAR file can contain privacy & security sensitive data and user-agents should find some way to notify the user of this fact before they transfer the file to anyone else.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Origin: evidence-derived control built to the documented sanitized shape; it is not a capture of a real Chrome export. All values are synthetic, built by hand from a documented grammar (a plain nonce or token under an obviously fake host and name) and were not tested against any service. HAR parsing, the decoding of a postData.text string, header coalescing, parser and action policy and product masking stay with the downstream repositories (credential-evidence#150, credential-eval).

relations.note: Same entry with the Cookie and Set-Cookie headers removed and the cookies arrays emptied; the credential values are absent rather than masked.
